channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Healthcare Sector Urged to Tackle Nicotine Addiction
item.description: A 2026 expert roundtable report calls for community pharmacies to play a central role in smoking cessation, arguing that the main challenge is delivering proven treatments consistently. Pharmacists can use routine consultations to give 30 seconds of advice and offer treatment or referral. The panel highlighted combination nicotine replacement therapy—a patch plus a faster-acting product—with behavioural support as a first-line option. It called for reliable referrals between pharmacies, GPs and hospitals, more consistent local commissioning, and compulsory undergraduate training in smoking cessation and nicotine dependence. (Published on November 25, 2026bypharmacy.biz)

item.title: Nicotine‑free vaping may still harm blood vessels – small MRI study
item.description: A small MRI study found that a single vaping session, with or without nicotine, altered blood flow and reduced oxygen levels in blood returning from the leg. Removing nicotine does not eliminate exposure to potentially harmful chemicals and metal particles in the aerosol. Earlier studies have reported impaired blood vessel function after vaping, though findings on nicotine-free vaping are mixed. The latest study measured only short-term effects and cannot establish whether repeated vaping causes lasting damage or increases the risk of heart attack or stroke. Vaping is less harmful than smoking, and nicotine-containing e-cigarettes can help smokers quit, but nicotine-free vaping is not risk-free. (Published on November 25, 2026bytheconversation.com)

item.title: Spain bans flavours for e-cigarettes and white snus – Artificial tobacco only flavour allowed
item.description: Spain has approved new restrictions on smoke-free nicotine products, permitting only artificial tobacco flavours in e-cigarettes and nicotine pouches, alongside a maximum nicotine content of 4mg per pouch. (Published on November 26, 2026byvejpkollen.se)

item.title: Kenya Should Not Jail Adults for Using Nicotine Pouches
item.description: Kenya is considering legislation that could impose up to ten years in prison or a KSh 5 million fine for using nicotine pouches, while conventional cigarettes would remain legally available. (Published on November 26, 2026bycenterforglobalhealthaccountability.org)

item.title: Bangladesh Smokeless Tobacco: The Oral Cancer Crisis
item.description: Around 22 million adults in Bangladesh use traditional smokeless tobacco products such as zarda, gul and sadapata, with use particularly prevalent among women. (Published on November 26, 2026bytobaccoharmreduction.net)
